observations: Service<RoleServer>::handle_request matches GetTaskRequest, UpdateTaskRequest and CancelTaskRequest separately. Each branch first calls validate_tasks_capability(self, &context), then calls the corresponding ServerHandler method with request.params and context by value.

The exact ServerHandler signatures are get_task(GetTaskParams, RequestContext<RoleServer>) -> Result<GetTaskResult, McpError>, update_task(UpdateTaskParams, RequestContext<RoleServer>) -> Result<(), McpError>, and cancel_task(CancelTaskParams, RequestContext<RoleServer>) -> Result<(), McpError>.

validate_tasks_capability checks server/client Tasks-extension capability only. The dispatcher does not establish task ownership or authenticated-principal binding before entering get_task/update_task/cancel_task.

Revision 81 already established from exact model.rs source that GetTaskParams, UpdateTaskParams and CancelTaskParams carry task_id and optional _meta, while UpdateTaskParams also carries InputResponses; no authenticated owner/principal field exists in those request parameter types.

required_security_order: Derive principal only from trusted server-side RequestContext provenance; never from request _meta.
Fail closed if trusted principal is absent or malformed.
Bind principal to request.task_id before any task-store read, input-response mutation, or cancellation mutation.
Only after ownership authorization perform the corresponding store operation.
Keep capability validation and ownership validation distinct: the SDK supplies the former dispatcher gate; the application must supply the latter.
